title: Classroom Story License Pack
audience: Elementary teachers, homeschool co-ops, tutors, and substitute folders serving reluctant writers ages 7-11.
sessionLength: 30 printable prompt cards, five classroom routines, ten extension activities, and a four-criterion rubric
safetyNote: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, no real child profiles.

cover.headline: Thirty story stations for one busy classroom
cover.subhead: Prompt cards, routines, extension activities, and a practical rubric for repeated short-story practice.
included: 30 prompt cards across setting, choice, sequence, dialogue, revision, sensory detail, problem-solution, ending, sentence variety, and peer sharing
Five classroom routines for launch, station rotation, quick conference, sentence share, and co-op circle
Five setup notes for preparing card trays, story maps, feedback sticky notes, and weekly focus cards
Ten extension activities for fast finishers, small groups, substitute folders, and co-op tables
Four-criterion rubric for concrete details, clear sequence, character choice, and revision move
Local image-backed world menu for visual station setup
Partner share moves that keep sharing low-pressure and specific
Printable source HTML for provider review
Offline teacher-facing language for paper-only classroom use
Reusable license-pack structure for future classroom bundles

classroomRoutines: Monday launch: read one prompt card, model a two-sentence story start, then let students draft privately for eight quiet minutes.
Station rotation: place four prompt cards at table groups for setting, problem, character choice, and revision so students collect one idea from each stop.
Quick conference line: while students write, meet with five students for one minute each and ask what changed because of the character's choice.
Friday sentence share: students choose one revised sentence to read to a partner, then name the detail they added or clarified.
Homeschool co-op circle: each child brings a finished paragraph, points to one concrete detail, and records one next-step revision before taking the page home.
teacherSetup: Print the prompt cards in small sets, cut them apart, and band each set by routine: warm-up, station, partner talk, or extension.
Prepare a class tray with blank story maps, half-page draft sheets, colored pencils, and sticky notes labeled add, move, replace, and explain.
Choose six cards for the week before class starts: two easy starters, two detail builders, one partner activity, and one fast-finisher challenge.
Post the four rubric words on the board with student-friendly reminders: details, order, choice, and revise.
Plan to score one rubric criterion per writing block so feedback stays fast, specific, and usable for the next draft.

extensionActivities.title: Detail Detective Walk
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Read one prompt card aloud, then send students to notice three classroom-safe details they can borrow for the setting.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: A three-item detail bank with one color, one texture, and one tiny action ready for a story draft.

extensionActivities.title: Sequence Strip Build
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Give pairs four blank strips and ask them to arrange a clear beginning, middle, choice, and ending before writing.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: A taped four-strip sequence plan with order words and one sentence on each strip.

extensionActivities.title: Choice Crossroads
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Pause after the story problem and chart two kind, practical choices the character could make.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: A short paragraph explaining the chosen path and one result that follows from it.

extensionActivities.title: Setting Sound Map
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Invite students to sketch a simple setting map and label quiet, busy, soft, and surprising sounds.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: A labeled setting map plus two sentences that use sound to make the scene clearer.

extensionActivities.title: Dialogue Tag Team
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Model one polite question and one helpful answer, then have partners build a tiny exchange for their characters.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: Four lines of dialogue with speaker names and one action tag that shows what a character is doing.

extensionActivities.title: Prop Card Sort
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Name five ordinary story objects and ask students to sort them into helpful, confusing, or clue categories.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: A three-column prop sort with one sentence explaining how one object changes the story.

extensionActivities.title: Revision Sticky Note
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Ask students to mark one draft spot with add, move, replace, or explain, then make only that revision.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: One revised sentence and a sticky note naming the exact revision move used.

extensionActivities.title: Ending Three Ways
extensionActivities.teacherMove: List three ending types: solve it, learn from it, or invite the next adventure, then let students test all three.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: Three possible endings for the same draft, with a star beside the clearest ending.

extensionActivities.title: Partner Question Pass
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Give each partner one question stem: What did the character notice, choose, change, or wonder?
extensionActivities.studentOutput: One partner question answered in writing and one draft detail improved because of it.

extensionActivities.title: Mini Conference Tracker
extensionActivities.teacherMove: Meet with small groups and record one rubric strength plus one next move for each student while the rest complete card-based drafting.
extensionActivities.studentOutput: A conference slip with one strength, one revision target, and a completed draft section.

criteria.name: Concrete details
criteria.lookFor: The draft includes observable nouns, actions, and sensory details a reader can picture without teacher explanation.

levels.Beginning: Names a place or object but gives few details the reader can picture.
levels.Developing: Adds one or two specific details, though some sentences still stay general.
levels.Secure: Uses several concrete details that make the setting, object, or action easy to imagine.
levels.Extending: Chooses precise details that also reveal mood, character thinking, or what matters in the scene.

criteria.name: Clear sequence
criteria.lookFor: The reader can follow what happens first, next, after the character's choice, and at the end.

levels.Beginning: Lists events or ideas, but the order is hard to follow.
levels.Developing: Shows a beginning and ending, with one middle event that may need a clearer connection.
levels.Secure: Organizes events in a clear order using time words, cause-and-effect, or paragraph flow.
levels.Extending: Controls pacing by slowing down the important choice and moving quickly through smaller steps.

criteria.name: Character choice
criteria.lookFor: The character makes a visible decision that changes what happens next in the story.

levels.Beginning: The character is present, but the story mostly happens around them.
levels.Developing: The character makes a choice, though the result is only partly explained.
levels.Secure: The character makes a clear choice and the next event follows from that decision.
levels.Extending: The choice shows what the character values and creates a more satisfying ending.

criteria.name: Revision move
criteria.lookFor: The student can point to a specific change made after rereading, feedback, or teacher conference.

levels.Beginning: Rereads the draft but makes no visible change yet.
levels.Developing: Fixes or adds a small part when prompted by the teacher or partner.
levels.Secure: Names and completes one useful revision move: add, move, replace, or explain.
levels.Extending: Makes a purposeful revision and can explain how it helps the reader understand the story.

promptCards.title: Acorn Avenue Setting Clues
promptCards.teacherSetup: Post this card at a writing station and ask students to circle one route choice before drafting.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Describe Acorn Avenue on a busy errand morning so a reader can picture where your helper is going.
writingLines: The first place my helper sees is ____________________
A tiny sign on the route says ____________________
One extra setting detail I will add is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask partners to point to the clearest place detail without correcting the draft.
promptCards.extension: Have students sketch a two-stop map and label one detail from their writing.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The draft includes at least two concrete place details that match the chosen route.

promptCards.title: Button Bakery Choice Helper
promptCards.teacherSetup: Give students thirty seconds to choose a bakery job before they write the scene.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a bakery helper who must choose the best way to fix a mixed-up crumb map.
writingLines: My helper notices the map problem when ____________________
The choice my helper makes is ____________________
Another choice my helper could try is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Invite students to read only the sentence that explains why the choice makes sense.
promptCards.extension: Students trade cards and list one kind consequence of a different choice.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing names a clear character choice and gives a reason for it.

promptCards.title: Teacup Town Forecast Order
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to number the three choices before completing the writing lines.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Create a Teacup Town forecast scene that shows what happens first, next, and last.
writingLines: Next, the town changes its plan by ____________________
After that, my character helps by ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Have partners hold up one, two, and three fingers as the sequence is read.
promptCards.extension: Students add a fourth step that still fits the order of the scene.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The draft uses sequence language to show events in a logical order.

promptCards.title: Pocket Park Notice Chat
promptCards.teacherSetup: Model one spoken line with quotation marks before students write their own park notice conversation.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a friendly conversation about which notice should go on the Pocket Park board first.
promptCards.shareMove: Let pairs read the two spoken lines quietly using classroom voices.
promptCards.extension: Students revise one line so it sounds more like the speaker who says it.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The dialogue includes two speakers and moves the notice-board problem forward.

promptCards.title: Penny Path Clearer Sentence
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to draft one quick direction sentence, then improve it with a clearer clue.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Help the compass shop owner revise a confusing direction into a sentence travelers can follow.
writingLines: I can make it clearer by adding ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask students to show a partner only the before-and-after change.
promptCards.extension: Students underline the exact words they added during revision.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The revised sentence is more specific than the first sentence.

promptCards.title: Rain Boot Route Sense Walk
promptCards.teacherSetup: Read the choices aloud and have students pick one sense to emphasize in their route description.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Describe a Rain Boot Route Rangers walk using safe sound, sight, or touch details.
writingLines: My route begins with this sound ____________________
The brightest thing I see is ____________________
The sensory detail that helps most is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Invite students to read one sensory phrase while classmates listen for the sense used.
promptCards.extension: Students add one color word and one texture word to the same scene.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing uses at least two sensory details connected to the route.

promptCards.title: Tidepool Lab Problem Fix
promptCards.teacherSetup: Have students mark P for problem and S for solution beside their lines after writing.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a tidepool lab note that does not match and how the timekeepers solve it calmly.
writingLines: The lab is ready again because ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask partners to identify the problem sentence and the solution sentence.
promptCards.extension: Students add a labeled diagram that shows the clue used to solve the problem.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing states a problem and a matching solution.

promptCards.title: Greenhouse Gear Ending Choice
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to choose the ending mood before drafting the final four lines.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write an ending for a greenhouse story where the helper decides what the gears should do next.
writingLines: At the end, the greenhouse helper chooses ____________________
The plants show the ending is working when ____________________
My final sentence will leave the reader thinking ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Let students name their ending mood before reading the final sentence.
promptCards.extension: Students write a second possible ending with a different mood.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The ending choice fits the greenhouse problem and gives the scene a clear finish.

promptCards.title: Pantry Measurement Sentence Mix
promptCards.teacherSetup: Write short, medium, and question on the board before students complete the pantry scene.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Tell a pantry mystery moment using different kinds of sentences so the writing does not sound the same each time.
writingLines: The sentence I like best is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask students to read two sentences and let a partner name how they are different.
promptCards.extension: Students reorder their sentences and choose which order sounds clearest.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The draft includes at least two sentence lengths or sentence types.

promptCards.title: Rain Gauge Railway Table Share
promptCards.teacherSetup: Use this card after a five-minute quickwrite and set a timer for quiet partner sharing.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Prepare one Rain Gauge Railway sentence you are comfortable sharing with a partner or small table group.
writingLines: The sentence I might share is ____________________
The part I want listeners to notice is ____________________
One question I can ask a partner is ____________________
One kind response I can give is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students may read one sentence, point to one line, or pass while still listening.
promptCards.extension: Students use one partner response to add a clearer rain or railway detail.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student prepares a shareable sentence and participates in a respectful response routine.

promptCards.title: Seed Drawer Map Details
promptCards.teacherSetup: Place three seed packets or blank index cards at the writing table and ask students to point to one map-room detail before they write.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Describe the seed library map room so a classmate can picture where the hidden garden note belongs.
writingLines: The first place I notice in the map room is ____________________
A tiny object on the table looks like ____________________
The map clue is tucked beside ____________________
My setting helps the story because ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask partners to trade papers and underline one detail they can picture clearly.
promptCards.extension: Students add a small map label in the margin and write one sentence explaining it.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student includes at least three concrete setting details tied to the story task.

promptCards.title: Solar Oven Picnic Fix
promptCards.teacherSetup: Draw a quick three-step test chart on the board with problem, try, and result columns.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Help the picnic team choose a fair fix when one solar oven warms a snack faster than the others.
writingLines: My hero tries this first fix: ____________________
The fair solution for the team is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Have students read only their solution sentence to a table partner.
promptCards.extension: Students sketch a before-and-after test card with one label for each change.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student names a clear problem and connects the solution to evidence from the scene.

promptCards.title: Moss Observatory Senses
promptCards.teacherSetup: Invite students to list quiet forest words for sight, touch, sound, and smell before drafting.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a calm observatory scene where moss details help your hero understand a nature message.
writingLines: The sensory clue tells my hero ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Invite volunteers to share one sensory word, not the whole paragraph.
promptCards.extension: Students revise one plain word into a more exact sensory word.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student uses sensory details that make the observatory scene more specific.

promptCards.title: Spoon Ferry Dock Dialogue
promptCards.teacherSetup: Model one polite question and one helpful answer on the board before students write their own lines.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a short dockside conversation that helps the spoon ferry deliver the right lunchbox order.
writingLines: The ferry cook asks this question: ____________________
My hero says this polite line: ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Partners read the three spoken lines in quiet voices and check whether the order makes sense.
promptCards.extension: Students add one action tag that shows who is speaking without using a name.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student writes dialogue that sounds polite and moves the scene forward.

promptCards.title: Museum Label Choice
promptCards.teacherSetup: Show students how a museum curator chooses one clue to place first and one clue to save for later.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Decide which exhibit label your curator should write first so visitors notice the best clue.
writingLines: My curator chooses the exhibit called ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students hold up one finger for first, second, or third clue choice before discussing with a partner.
promptCards.extension: Students write a second version of the label for younger museum visitors.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student explains a character choice with a reason connected to the visitor experience.

promptCards.title: Compass Craft Route Order
promptCards.teacherSetup: Give students three sticky notes or paper scraps so they can physically order the route before writing.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Plan the order of stops for a craft-academy map route that leads to a finished story project.
writingLines: First, my map route goes to ____________________
The final stop is important because ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students compare only their first and final stops with a nearby writer.
promptCards.extension: Students add transition words above each line and read the route again.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student uses ordered steps that make the route easy to follow.

promptCards.title: Almost Invention Sentence Test
promptCards.teacherSetup: Write a short sentence, a longer because sentence, and a question sentence on the board as examples.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Test an almost-invention by writing sentences that do not all start or sound the same.
promptCards.shareMove: Ask students to star the sentence type they used least and share that one with a partner.
promptCards.extension: Students combine two short sentences into one smoother sentence.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student tries at least three sentence patterns while staying on the same invention idea.

promptCards.title: Binding Day Ending Choice
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to choose whether their booklet ending should feel helpful, funny, or thoughtful before they write.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write an ending for Binding Day that shows how the finished booklet is shared in the classroom.
writingLines: At the boardwalk table, the finished booklet shows ____________________
My hero chooses to end with ____________________
The final sentence of my story is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students read their final sentence only and let partners name the ending feeling.
promptCards.extension: Students draft a second ending with a different feeling and circle the stronger one.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student writes an ending that matches the story action and leaves a clear final feeling.

promptCards.title: Index Card Theater Table Share
promptCards.teacherSetup: Arrange students in pairs and give each writer one index card for a scene title or favorite line.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Prepare a tiny theater-club share that lets a partner understand your scene without reading the whole story.
writingLines: One line I can share is ____________________
One prop or action that helps is ____________________
A kind question for my partner is ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Partners share one card each, then say one thing they understood clearly.
promptCards.extension: Students add a tiny cue mark where a reader should pause.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student selects a short shareable piece and responds to a peer with a kind question or comment.

promptCards.title: Revision River Two-Pass
promptCards.teacherSetup: Tell students to pick one sentence from yesterday or from a quick draft and copy it onto the first line.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Ride the revision ferry by changing one sentence so it becomes clearer and more interesting.
writingLines: The revision move I chose is ____________________
The revised version is clearer because ____________________
promptCards.shareMove: Students point to the changed word or phrase instead of reading the whole draft aloud.
promptCards.extension: Students make one more small revision and label it with the move they used.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student makes a visible revision and can explain how the change improves the sentence.

promptCards.title: Moon Muffin Market Stall Details
promptCards.teacherSetup: Place this card at a description station and ask students to add three market details before drafting.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a moonlit muffin stall where your character notices one detail that helps the whole market run smoothly.
promptCards.shareMove: Invite students to read only their strongest setting detail to a partner.
promptCards.extension: Have students circle one vague word and replace it with a more exact market detail.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing includes at least three concrete setting details tied to the market scene.

promptCards.title: Puddle Planet Delivery Choice
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to pick one delivery decision and explain why the character chooses it.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a post office on Puddle Planet where your character must choose the fairest way to sort a mixed-up stack of cheerful notes.
writingLines: One reason for this choice is ________________________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask partners to name the choice they heard and one reason that made sense.
promptCards.extension: Add a thought bubble that shows what the character considers before deciding.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing names a clear character choice and gives a reason connected to the scene.

promptCards.title: Buttonwood Library Train Sequence
promptCards.teacherSetup: Have students number the four writing lines before they draft so the events stay in order.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write the order of events as a tiny library train carries book carts to the right reading rooms.
promptCards.shareMove: Have students swap cards and point to the word that shows each step in order.
promptCards.extension: Add one transition word to each line without changing the order.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing uses a clear beginning, middle steps, and ending in logical order.

promptCards.title: Cloudberry Clocktower Polite Dialogue
promptCards.teacherSetup: Model one line of polite dialogue, then have students write two speakers with different jobs.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a short conversation at Cloudberry Clocktower where two helpers calmly decide how to reset the snack-time chimes.
promptCards.shareMove: Let pairs read the dialogue quietly, each taking one speaker's line.
promptCards.extension: Revise one line so it sounds more like the speaker's job.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The dialogue includes at least two speakers and moves the clocktower problem forward.

promptCards.title: Tiny Lantern Reef Revision Dive
promptCards.teacherSetup: Give students a first sentence to improve and ask them to revise for clarity rather than length.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Revise a reef scene so readers can understand how the tiny lanterns guide a friendly sea parade.
writingLines: I can make it clearer by adding ________________________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask students to share the one word or detail they changed, not the whole draft.
promptCards.extension: Use a colored pencil to underline the added revision detail.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student identifies a specific change and improves clarity in the revised sentence.

promptCards.title: Pencil Dragon Academy Sense Notes
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to use at least two senses before writing the academy scene.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a Pencil Dragon Academy lesson where careful sense details help a student remember the next writing step.
promptCards.shareMove: Invite students to trade cards and star one sensory detail they can picture clearly.
promptCards.extension: Add one more sense detail to the line that feels thinnest.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing uses two or more sensory details that fit the academy setting.

promptCards.title: Margin Note Market Problem Fix
promptCards.teacherSetup: Have students state the market problem in one sentence before choosing a calm solution.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a market in the margins of a notebook where tiny notes get out of order and your character finds a fair fix.
promptCards.shareMove: Ask volunteers to read only the problem and solution lines as a quick pair check.
promptCards.extension: Draw a before-and-after margin note to show how the fix changes the market.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing connects a specific problem to a specific solution that fits the notebook market.

promptCards.title: Pocket Park Notice Board Ending
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to draft two possible endings and choose the one that best matches the park notice.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write an ending for a pocket park story where the final notice helps everyone understand the shared plan.
promptCards.shareMove: Let students hold up one or two fingers to show which ending they chose before explaining.
promptCards.extension: Add a final sentence that shows how the park feels after the notice is read.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The chosen ending matches the earlier story problem and explains why it fits.

promptCards.title: Greenhouse Gear Garden Sentence Mix
promptCards.teacherSetup: Display short, medium, and question sentence examples before students draft the greenhouse note.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a greenhouse gear note using different kinds of sentences so the garden helpers can follow the plan.
writingLines: A longer sentence with a detail: ________________________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask partners to tap once for a short sentence and twice for a longer sentence.
promptCards.extension: Revise one sentence beginning so not every line starts the same way.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing includes varied sentence lengths or types that remain clear.

promptCards.title: Solar Oven Picnic Station Share Card
promptCards.teacherSetup: Set a two-minute partner share and remind students to respond with one noticed detail and one question.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a picnic station scene you can share with a partner, showing how the solar oven team prepares a fair test snack.
writingLines: A detail I want my partner to notice is ________________________________
A question I can ask my partner is ________________________________
promptCards.shareMove: Partners give one quiet compliment about a clear detail and ask one curious question.
promptCards.extension: Add a peer suggestion box where the writer can choose one idea to try next.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student prepares a shareable scene and includes a specific detail for peer response.
